title: TOEFL PREPARATION COURSE
overview: The TOEFL Preparation Course develops the academic English proficiency and test-taking skills required for the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), with particular emphasis on the TOEFL iBT. Participants build competence in reading academic texts, understanding lectures and conversations, communicating ideas in spoken English, and producing clear written responses. Guided practice, integrated-skills tasks, timed assessments, and individualized feedback help learners identify performance gaps and improve confidence under examination conditions.
audience: Students applying to English-medium universities and colleges.
Graduates seeking admission to postgraduate or professional programs.
Professionals requiring evidence of academic English proficiency.
Learners preparing for the TOEFL iBT who need structured skills development and exam practice.
methodology: Instructor-led instruction combines diagnostic testing, academic language workshops, guided analysis of authentic-style tasks, listening and reading drills, speaking recordings, timed writing, integrated-skills simulations, peer review, and targeted instructor feedback. Participants complete regular practice tasks and mock examinations, followed by individual improvement planning. Test format and task types are reviewed against the official requirements applicable to the participant’s examination date.
competencies: Academic reading comprehension and evidence-based interpretation.
Listening comprehension, selective note-taking, and synthesis of academic information.
Clear spoken responses with logical organization, intelligibility, and appropriate language use.
Academic writing, idea development, coherence, and language accuracy.
Integrated reading, listening, speaking, and writing performance.
Test strategy, time management, self-monitoring, and performance improvement.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the TOEFL iBT test structure, scoring principles, and task expectations.
Read academic passages efficiently and answer comprehension questions using textual evidence.
Identify main ideas, supporting details, speaker purpose, and relationships in spoken academic English.
Take useful notes and synthesize information across sources.
Deliver organized spoken responses with relevant support and controlled pacing.
Produce coherent written responses that address task requirements and use appropriate academic language.
Apply timing, checking, and stress-management strategies during practice examinations.
Interpret feedback and create an individual study plan based on demonstrated weaknesses.
